In a reinforcement learning rollout serving system with disaggregated prefill and decode workers, scheduling is optimized by dynamically assigning tasks to independent prefill and decode workers to minimize idle time and resource overlap. Cache behavior ensures efficient data reuse, reducing memory overhead and latency. Tail latency is minimized by decoupling the prefill and decode processes, allowing for asynchronous processing. Request migration facilitates load balancing by moving tasks between workers, improving throughput. Role switching enables dynamic resource allocation, which enhances flexibility and adaptability. GPU utilization is balanced through efficient allocation of compute resources, while throughput tradeoffs involve balancing between processing power, cache efficiency, and request handling speed to optimize overall performance. This design maximizes system efficiency by decoupling tasks and prioritizing resource flexibility.
